title: La Golondrina - Galveston canto guide
composer: Narciso Serradell Sevilla (standard attribution; Galveston print leaves composer and arranger unnamed)
edition: Thos. Goggan & Bro., Galveston, plate 29512. Copyright 1883 by L. W. Stevenson, Laredo. Cover dated March 1889.
scope: Editorial monophonic reading of the texted upper staff on printed pp. 2–3, aligned to the Galveston piano left hand.
editorial: The print sets lyrics beneath a harmonized treble staff. Follow its upper line in sung passages, taking the lower A4 in the refrain's fourth and fifth half-note chords as the sung line.

Use eight-tick eighth-note triplets for the three groups after the refrain's opening quarter, the six attacks after its third bar's two quarters, and the six attacks after its fifth bar's half note. Beam grouping and the common-time bar length inform this reading.

The guide is silent through the instrumental introduction and coda, except for the printed vocal pickup into the verse. The four untexted sixteenths in the refrain's second ending lead into the instrumental coda and are omitted from the guide.
Unmeasured grace notes are omitted and fermatas use nominal duration. Preserve the vocal pickups in the verse first ending, verse second ending and refrain first ending.
Alberto Grau's later choral setting was consulted for voice separation in the harmonized treble. All guide events and the form derive from the Galveston print.
